commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: ci: deploy the hosted app on every merge to main, as the staging surface
commits.body:
#74 moved this to `v*` tags so the public web app and the public APK told the same story.
That reasoning assumed the hosted app was a distribution channel. It is more useful as a
staging one: the value of having it is trying what just landed on a real phone against a
real server, and waiting for a release defeats that.

So the trigger goes back to `push` on `main` filtered to `web/**`, and the tag trigger is
dropped rather than kept alongside it — a release commit reaches main anyway, so the tag
would only ever redeploy the same tree. `workflow_dispatch` stays for a redeploy from any
ref.

The two channels are now deliberately different rather than accidentally so: the APK is
release-only and is what people install; the URL follows main and is what we test. The
README says which is which, so nobody installs the wrong one by accident.

The six web suites stay ahead of the build, and matter more under this trigger than under
the previous one: deploying every merge is only safe if a merge that breaks them cannot
reach the URL.

Workflow YAML re-parsed: triggers are `workflow_dispatch` and `push` on `main` filtered to
`web/**` plus the workflow file itself.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix: stop claiming to load models a harness does not have, and hide injected turns
commits.body:
Both found while driving the Claude Code backend from the hosted app.

**"Loading configured models..." forever.** `loadModels` returns early when
`capabilities.models` is false, so on a harness without a model list nothing is ever
fetched — and every place that reports progress treated an empty list as a fetch still in
flight. The Claude Code backend has `models: false`, so its AI panel and status chip sat on
the loading text for the life of the session, reading as a hang in a feature that is simply
absent. There are three states, not two: nothing to load, loading, failed. Named the first.

**Harness bookkeeping shown as the user's own words.** Verified against the live bridge:
of the messages in an active session, two contained a `<task-notification>` block and both
were recorded `role=user`. A harness that injects notifications and reminders into the
model's context sends them as user turns, and the adapter forwards them as
`user_message_chunk` — correctly, at the protocol level. Rendered as-is, the app attributes
harness internals to the person holding the phone: text they never wrote, and which does
not appear in the harness's own view of the session.

Suppressed, but only when a chunk is *entirely* one or more such blocks. The report that
surfaced this was itself a message quoting one while asking about it, and that has to stay
visible — so the regex anchors both ends and a message with any prose around the block is
kept. Covered both ways in the bridge suite.

The pinned expression in the existing "a failed model fetch must be named" assertion had to
loosen: it matched the whole two-state label, and now asserts the failure branch alone so a
third state does not break it again.

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: feat: offer Claude Code's models, which the bridge had been discarding
commits.body:
The backend carried `models: false` because it appeared to expose none. It exposes five.
Asked the adapter directly over stdio: `session/new` returns a `model` config option with
`currentValue: "default"` and options for Default, Sonnet, Fable, Opus (1M context) and
Haiku — the same shape OMP and PI use, and the same `model` id the bridge already looks for.

What differed is the naming. The app's model API is OpenCode's, where a model is
`provider/model`, and the response builder split on "/" and skipped anything without both
halves. Claude Code's ids carry no provider — `sonnet`, `opus[1m]` — so every option hit
that `continue` and the endpoint answered `{"providers":[],"default":{}}`. Nothing was
missing; we were dropping it.

A bare id is now presented under the backend's own name, so it reads and behaves like the
others: `claude/sonnet`. Going the other way, `setModel` resolves against the options the
agent actually offered — exact match first, then the part after the synthesised provider —
rather than trusting either spelling. `provider/model` harnesses match exactly and never
reach the fallback, which is pinned by its own test.

Verified against the real adapter through the bridge, both directions: five models listed
under provider `claude` with their proper names, `claude/haiku` accepted, the agent
answered, and the current model then read back as `haiku`.

+    assert.equal(body.providers.length, 1, "bare ids must not be discarded")
+    const provider = body.providers[0]
+    assert.equal(provider.id, "claude", "a bare id is presented under the backend's own name")
+    assert.equal(provider.name, "claude")
+    assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(provider.models).sort(), ["default", "opus[1m]", "sonnet"])
+    assert.equal(provider.models.sonnet.name, "Sonnet")
+    assert.equal(body.default[provider.id], "default", "the current model is reported as the default")
+
+    // The app sends back the pair it was given; the agent must receive the original ACP value.
+    const prompted = await fetch(`${bridge.baseURL}/session/session-1/prompt_async`, {
+      method: "POST",
+      headers: jsonHeaders(),
+      body: JSON.stringify({ parts: [{ type: "text", text: "hello" }], model: { providerID: provider.id, modelID: "opus[1m]" } })
+    })
+    assert.equal(prompted.status, 200)
+    await new Promise((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve))
+    assert.deepEqual(acp.models, ["opus[1m]"], "a bare id must not be re-joined into provider/model")
+  } finally {
+    await bridge.close()
+  }
+})
+
+test("keeps provider/model values untouched for the harnesses that use them", async () => {
+  const acp = new HeldTurnOmpAcp()
+  const bridge = await startServer({ acp })
+  try {
+    const listed = await fetch(`${bridge.baseURL}/config/providers?sessionID=session-1`, { headers: authHeaders() })
+    const body = await listed.json()
+    assert.equal(body.providers[0].id, "omp", "a value with a provider part still yields that provider")
+    assert.equal(body.providers[0].name, "omp")
+    assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(body.providers[0].models).sort(), ["first", "second"])
+  } finally {
+    await bridge.close()
+  }
+})

commits.subject: feat: show which Sonnet, by keeping the description the harness sends
commits.body:
The picker listed "Sonnet", "Haiku", "Opus (1M context)" with no version, while the desktop
client shows "Sonnet 5", "Haiku 4.5". The version was never missing: the adapter sends it in
each option's `description` — "Haiku 4.5 · Fastest for quick answers" — and the response
builder kept only id, name and status.

Passed through and given the picker's secondary line, which until now held the provider
name. That line earned its place when the provider distinguished something; with one
synthesised provider it read "claude" on all five rows while the useful text stayed
invisible. The provider still fills it for a harness that describes nothing, so OpenCode,
OMP and PI look exactly as before — pinned by an assertion that OMP's models come back with
no description rather than an empty one.

`description` is optional the whole way through: OpenCode's own API has no such field, so
nothing is claimed of a harness that does not offer it.

Verified against the real adapter: all five models arrive with their versions, from
"Sonnet 5 · Efficient for routine tasks" to "Fable 5 · Most capable for your hardest and
longest-running tasks · Requires usage credits".

bridge: 52/52. web: clean build, 6/6 suites.
